aspects.says: A direct network link needs the channel whose frame matches the specification; VAPChannel adds two zero bytes and a 22-byte BASE I header after the length.
basis: section:5.5.1 The Link Speaks the Network's Framing

aspects.says: Field 43 is read by position, so each part is cut and padded to the width the specification gives it.
basis: section:5.2.2 Field 43 Has Positions, Not Separators

aspects.says: Per-network values such as the acquirer ID come from configuration, and a missing one must stop the request, because ISOMsg.set with null silently removes the field.
basis: section:5.2 The Network Shows Up as Configuration, and a Missing Value Stops the Request
section:5.2.1 Spot the Problem: The Mastercard Launch

aspects.says: A QMUX does not route; each network's requests go through that network's MUX only, and a down link means host unavailable, never another network's link.
basis: section:5.5 Each Network Is a Destination of Its Own

aspects.says: The fields ISO 8583 defines read the same on every network, so one builder makes them with the network as a parameter; per-network copies drift.
basis: section:5.1 One Builder Makes What Every Network Shares

aspects.says: Private-use fields are defined only by each network's licensed specification and are kept behind one hook per network, never filled from a guess.
basis: section:5.4 Private Fields Come From the Network's Specification, Behind One Hook

aspects.says: Field 22 and the card fields 14, 35 and 55 come from one value describing how the card was read, so a request never claims a read its data contradicts.
basis: section:5.3 How the Card Was Read Decides the Card Fields
